summary: The video side is built as the board's own scan-time circuitry. There is a 74161 counter chain for the raster, the sprite unit finds visible sprites during HBLANK into an address stack and is sequenced by an emulated timing PROM, and two ping-pong 4-bit line buffers are cleared after readout. ROMs and buffers are named by board location (S8/U8/R8/N8/H5/K5/F10/U2/T2). Nothing mirrors MAME's tilemap callbacks, its frame-wide sprite loop or its ROM[HL] protection hack. The one clear MAME carry-over is the colour-intensity table, whose values match MAME's palette_init resistor weights.

findings.where: rtl/video_timing.v:58-160 (ttl161 v4/w4/j3/h3, ttl74 w9_a), rtl/ttl161.v, rtl/ttl74.v
findings.note: H and V come from cascaded 161 counters with carry/load and preload data built from HX and K3 flip-flop outputs, and VBL is preset by the G3 NAND. MAME only gives raw screen parameters.

findings.signal: per-line sprite search into address stack
findings.note: During HBLANK the A7 counter steps through sprite Y bytes, and visible entries (j7 = Y+V+1, high nibble zero) are pushed into a 15-deep stack indexed by A9. A9 then counts down as each sprite is drawn. MAME instead loops over all sprites per frame in reverse order.

A free-running H10 counter (LS393) decodes the PAD/PIC address phases, shift-register load strobes and the A9 decrement for an 8-clock-per-sprite slot. These are board timing phases, not C control flow.

findings.signal: ping-pong sprite line buffers with clear-on-read
findings.note: Buffers F8/G8 swap roles on V[0]. One buffer's counter is loaded from sprite X and written only when the pixel is non-zero; the other is read and then zeroed, the way pull-downs on the PCB clear it. This is a per-pixel scan-time pipeline.

findings.signal: sprite colour lookup PROM in pixel path
findings.note: Sprite pixels go through the F10 PROM, addressed by {colour[2:0], pixel bits}, as they are shifted out of the K6/J6 nibble shifters, with colour[3] picking the nibble. MAME folds this into its pen-indirect table at init time.

findings.signal: tile shift registers loaded on H[2:0]
findings.note: Tile RAM is fetched at H=5, the bitmap ROM address is formed at H=6 and the shifters are loaded at H=7 from ROMs U8/S8/N8/R8. Flip is handled by bit-reversing on load. There are no tile_info callbacks or tilemap objects.
Memories and logic are named by PCB location (cpu ROMs a4/c4/e4/f4, gfx s8/u8/r8/n8/h5/k5, PROMs u2/t2/f10, counters h10/a7/a9/k6/j6, pal u001), not by MAME region names like gfx1/gfx2/proms.

findings.signal: protection PAL modelled independently of MAME
findings.note: U001 is a registered latch clocked by FG tile-RAM writes, using an observed input-to-output table with an internal mode bit. MAME's mrdo protection_r is a ROM[HL] hack, so this is not taken from MAME.

findings.signal: palette intensity constants equal MAME's computed weights
findings.note: The 16-entry table {0,0,0,88,0,112,133,192,60,150,166,212,180,221,229,255} is exactly the weight[] array MAME computes from its resistor/diode model (MAME gives 254 for the last entry), indexed {U2 bits, T2 bits} the same way.
Sprite over FG over BG, with attr bit 6 forcing a layer opaque. Any correct implementation shares this semantics; here it is evaluated per pixel.
The range-compare decode matches the memory map, as any correct core must. The 0xF000 scroll-X register is left out.
